prompts:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
Image 1 is the edit target: the wide AMIGA GAME KIT pixel-art demoscene banner.
Image 2 is the user's physical proportions and perspective reference: an actual Commodore Amiga 500 photographed obliquely.
Edit ONLY the beige Amiga computer in the lower-left foreground and its immediate shadow. The current computer is too front-facing and too deep/tall. Replace it with a properly proportioned, broad, shallow, low-profile Amiga 500 seen at a much stronger three-quarter angle. Use the HORIZONTALLY OPPOSITE VIEWPOINT to the reference photo: camera above and to the computer's FRONT LEFT, rather than the reference photo's front-right. The nearest front-left corner is low in the image, the front edge recedes clearly diagonally upward toward the right, and the computer's left side is clearly visible at image-left. Match the strong diagonal foreshortening and low camera elevation of the reference, reversed in viewpoint. This must be a visibly significant rotation, not a slight tweak to the current near-frontal view.
Use the actual reference's physical proportions: very wide chassis relative to depth, thin shallow sloping wedge, restrained rear rise, broad low front lip, no exaggerated towering rear panel or chunky tall case. Fit the whole computer into roughly the existing lower-left foreground region, with a little breathing room at the canvas edge.
Reverse the viewpoint, NOT the hardware: keep the genuine A500 keyboard topology, normal unmirrored readable AMIGA case logo, full QWERTY block at the machine's left, separated Esc and two groups of five function keys, long spacebar, Del and Help, inverted-T arrows, numeric keypad at the machine's RIGHT, accurate upper rear vents and right-side status LEDs. Do not mirror the keyboard or put the floppy drive on the left side. Follow the user's reference photograph carefully for the case and keys. The computer should look like a pixel-art depiction of this actual product viewed from the opposite side.
Render with the same crisp deliberate pixel clusters, stepped shading, beige plastic, warm sunset rim light and violet contact shadows as the banner. No photorealistic pasted-in object. Preserve everything else in image 1: the exact banner dimensions and layout, all title and subtitle typography and wording, checkered ball, spacecraft, mountains, sunset, lake, castle, colours, and background pixels. No new accessories, labels or other text.

Use case: precise-object-edit. Edit this existing banner with an extremely localized correction ONLY.
The Amiga 500 computer in the lower left now has the desired angle and proportions. Keep its position, size, perspective, keyboard, numeric keypad, case logo, vents and lighting EXACTLY unchanged.
The one error is the black floppy-drive slot and eject button on the visible LEFT SIDE of the computer, at the far left edge of the banner. The real Amiga 500 floppy drive is on the RIGHT SIDE, which is hidden from this camera. REMOVE the black drive slot, eject button and drive details from the visible left-side panel. Replace only that tiny side-panel area with matching solid beige plastic and the subtle outline of the real A500 left expansion-port cover, a CLOSED plain rectangular cover, no open black slot, no button. Preserve the shallow case seam and its violet shadow. Do not add a drive elsewhere.
Change no other pixels or composition. In particular preserve the strong three-quarter front-left view, full keyboard layout, all banner lettering, background, ball and landscape.
description: Selected demoscene banner, revised against actual Amiga 500 photographs for case proportions and a front-left three-quarter perspective.
